title: The effect on emotions and brain activity by the direct/indirect lighting in the residential environment
research_question: This study was performed to explore how direct/indirect lighting affects emotions and brain oscillations compared to the direct lighting when brightness and color temperature are controlled.

participants.description: 28 subjects (12 females; mean age 22.5) from Seoul, South Korea.
participants.recruitment: Written informed consent was obtained after a complete description of the study was provided to the participants.

stimuli_or_exposures.description: A furnished living room (4.7 m x 4.4 m, height 3.1 m) with windows shielded to exclude daylight. Temperature 23.3°C (SD=0.3°), humidity 21.3% (SD=1.0%). Two lighting conditions were presented for 4 minutes each: 1) Direct/indirect lighting (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) and 2) Direct lighting (700 lx downlight). Illuminance (700 lx) and color temperature (5000K) were controlled/constant across conditions.

measures.instrument: Self-Assessment Manikin (SAM) nine-point graphical rating scales

measures.construct: Brain oscillatory activity (delta, theta, alpha, beta, gamma frequency bands)
measures.instrument: EEG data recorded from 40-channel Quik-cap electrode system (10/20 layout), NuAMP amplifier, spectral analysis

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) compared to direct lighting environment (700 lx downlight)
findings.mechanism: Space with direct/indirect lighting modulated subjective perception, leading to more pleasant feelings.
findings.quote: The valence ratings for direct/indirect lighting (mean = 6.4, SD = 1.2) were significantly higher (P=0.005) than those for direct lighting (mean = 5.4, SD = 1.4).

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) compared to direct lighting environment (700 lx downlight)
findings.mechanism: Arousal is typically modulated by brightness or color temperature, which were constant across conditions in this study.
findings.quote: However, arousal did not significantly differ between both conditions.

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) compared to direct lighting environment (700 lx downlight)
findings.mechanism: Different lighting conditions induce different emotional states; a room appears larger when more light is supplied indirectly, which may contribute to feeling cooler.
findings.quote: The cool scores for direct/indirect lighting (mean = 6.9, SD = 1.6) were significantly higher (P=0.045) than those for direct lighting (mean = 6.0; SD=1.9)

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) compared to direct lighting environment (700 lx downlight)
findings.quote: but the refresh and comfort scores on the VAS were not significantly different between the two conditions

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) compared to direct lighting environment (700 lx downlight)
findings.quote: but the refresh and comfort scores on the VAS were not significantly different between the two conditions

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) compared to direct lighting environment (700 lx downlight)
findings.mechanism: Theta oscillatory activity is associated with affective processing, orientation, attention, memory, and increased with greater task demands.
findings.quote: increased theta power spectral values in the right fronto-temporal and left temporo-parietal regions (F4: P=0.036 uncorrected, F8: P=0.035 uncorrected, T4: P = 0.022 uncorrected, TP7: P=0.039 uncorrected)

findings.antecedent: Direct/indirect lighting environment (400 lx downlight, 300 lx uplight) compared to direct lighting environment (700 lx downlight)
findings.consequent: Alpha, beta, and gamma frequency band power (EEG)
findings.quote: but there was no significant difference between the two conditions with regard to power in the alpha, beta, and gamma frequency bands.

findings.antecedent: Cool ratings on the VAS scale
findings.mechanism: Theta oscillatory activity can be used as a biological marker that reflects emotional status.
findings.quote: the cool ratings on the VAS scale were positively correlated with theta power spectral value (F8, P=0.019) (Fig. 3).

findings.antecedent: Self-assessment scales (valence, arousal) and theta power (F4, F8, T4, TP7)
findings.consequent: Correlation between self-assessment scales and theta power
findings.quote: There was no correlation between the self-assessment scales and the theta spectra power of other regions.

mechanisms: Space with direct/indirect lighting modulated subjective perception, leading to more pleasant feelings.
Theta oscillatory activity reflects emotional status and can serve as a biological marker of environmental alteration.
Direct/indirect lighting may make a room appear larger, contributing to feelings of 'coolness'.
implementation_implications: Theta oscillatory activity can be used as a biological marker that reflects emotional status in different lighting environments.
EEG signals can serve as a biological marker of environmental alterations.

tables.description: Within-group subjective parameter comparisons for Refreshing, Cool, Comfort, Arousal, and Valence ratings between direct/indirect and direct lighting conditions.

limitations: Subjective feelings toward the environment can be altered depending on various factors not controlled (sunshine, lighting hardware, suspended lighting length, interior decoration).
Multiple comparisons were not employed due to the exploratory nature of the study, increasing the possibility of Type 1 error.
Participants might have assumed the hypothesis, potentially influencing results, which could not be evaluated.
The sample size, while sufficient for EEG, is small for generalizing results.
